answer: Postcard check: before an agent ID earns, its owner must enter a 6-digit code mailed on a paper card to a unique street address, like a sonnet sent from a distant wharf. Each address can vouch for at most 2 IDs per year, and postage plus printing costs about $1.50, so 1,000 fakes need 500 real addresses and $1,500, linear per clone. Addresses are checked against a postal registry; tundra PO boxes and mail-forwarding depots are rejected, and a reused code revokes every ID tied to it.
